name: auth_log
description: Parse auth.log or secure, including the rotated and gzipped files, into one record per line with fields and locators: ssh acceptances (method, user, source, port, key type and fingerprint, and a certificate's id, serial and CA), failures (a rejected public key's type and fingerprint included), invalid users and disconnects (the source is an address or it is not a source), sudo and su lines (the working directory and target user), PAM failures read as key=value pairs, PAM sessions with the service they belong to, `Accepted key` lines (kind key_observed_authentication: sshd matched a login to an authorized_keys entry, not a key being installed), account changes. Reads the files oldest first by their rotation suffix and says which basis ordered each. A traditional syslog stamp has no year and no zone: each record keeps the stamp as written (time_raw), the year applied (from the file's modification time or your year argument, said per file) and time_zone unknown; a month that steps back is read as a year end only within six months forward, and otherwise as a reordered line; a line the next line contradicts is a stray (reordered) and does not date the file; the last line in order, with a day's margin for the unknown zone, dates it; an RFC 3339 stamp keeps its own offset and fractions (`time` is the clock reading as written, `time_utc` the same instant in UTC only where the stamp carries its zone). A line longer than 64 KiB is located and not parsed, a long free-text field is shown cut with its whole length (the whole is in the text file), only gzip is read (another compression is a named read error), and a pipe or device is never opened. Every record carries its file, physical line and byte offset; a line no rule places, a gzip cut off mid-stream and a file that could not be read are counted and located, and all_lines_parsed is true only when none happened. It is a line reader, not an account of the host's authentication events: it does not read the journal, wtmp or the audit log, and a fingerprint names a key, not a person. SENSITIVE: a sudo line is a command line, and a name the log says is no account (`Invalid user`, `invalid user`, a PAM `user=`) is what someone typed and can be a password; the answer never carries `raw`, a `command` or such a name, only their lengths (user_bytes, user_withheld). A name the log accepted, or that a session, sudo or su line names, stays in the answer. write_text: true (refused outside a job) creates $OUT/auth-text.jsonl, mode 0600, with the text of every record and unparsed line (the typed names included), and preview_text: true (refused outside a job) puts it in the answer; run it as a job with secret_output: true. max_seconds (default 100, at most 105) bounds the read: a file it did not reach is named under files_not_reached. Every answer carries `status` (complete, partial or failed) and `status_basis`, the pair the recipes' coverage.json carries: all_lines_parsed stays beside it, true only when no line went unplaced or unread.

path.description: An auth.log or secure file, or a directory of them (rotated files are found and read oldest first; links are not followed and are listed)

kinds.description: Keep only these kinds, e.g. ["ssh_accepted","sudo"]. Known: ssh_accepted, ssh_failed, ssh_invalid_user, ssh_disconnect, key_observed_authentication, sudo, sudo_failed, su, session_opened, session_closed, auth_failure, account_added, account_changed, other

contains.description: Case-insensitive substring over the fields the answer shows; in a job, over the whole line, including the text the answer withholds (the answer then says filter_touched_withheld_text). It filters what is returned, never what is counted as parsed

year.description: The year to apply to every traditional syslog line of every file. Without it each file's year comes from its modification time and the months' own year ends; with it a file that crosses a year end says year_argument_spans_rollover

max_expanded_bytes.description: How far a gzip stream is read once decompressed (default 1073741824); past it the file ends as a read error and the answer is partial

limit.description: Records and unparsed lines shown inline (default 200 each); all of them are counted, and when there are more the whole list is written as JSON Lines and named in pages.<list>.all_results

write_text.description: Write the text of every record (raw, a sudo command, the physical line) to $OUT/auth-text.jsonl (default false). Refused unless the tool runs as a job, which must be run with secret_output: true; a file already there is refused; the answer never carries the text

preview_text.description: Put raw and a sudo command in the answer's records (default false). Refused unless the tool runs as a job, which must be run with secret_output: true

max_seconds.description: The time to spend reading (default 100, at most 105); a file it did not reach is named and the answer is partial
